## Re-review returned BLOCK; all 4 findings were correct. Fixed, re-review running.

The earlier attestation was `stale-material` — my own AC5 rewrite and `file_impact`
declaration staled it. Re-running the review surfaced 4 findings, 1 blocking. I verified
each against the tree before editing rather than taking them on assertion; all 4 hold.

### Finding 1 — BLOCKING (priority 0.889, threshold 0.8). Correct.

AC4 named the corpus as `eval_specs/code-review-tests.eval.yaml`. There is no top-level
`eval_specs/` directory — `ls eval_specs` returns "No such file or directory". The real path
is `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/code-review-tests.eval.yaml`.

The reviewer also diagnosed the origin correctly: the bare form is an abbreviation inside the
`criteria_routing.json` `_comment`, which this plan quotes. The quote is faithful; the error
was promoting an abbreviation into an AC as a literal edit target.

**Fixed in AC4 only.** The blockquote at the "Why the verification route is the eval corpus"
section still reads `eval_specs/...` because it reproduces the `_comment` verbatim, and the
reviewer explicitly scoped the fix to edit targets while leaving quoted text intact.

### Finding 3 — advisory. Correct.

The AC4-kind mapping table cited `change-detector (":58" …)`. Verified: the change-detector
entry spans `code-review-tests.md:23-26` with the quoted phrase at `:24`; line 58 sits inside
the fail-open-oracle entry. The reviewer's own note is right that the substantive claim —
refactor mechanics is already covered — is TRUE, so only the anchor was wrong. Corrected to
`:23-26`, phrase at `:24`.

### Finding 2 — advisory. Correct, and now has a named owner.

AC5's offline test checks the corpus's structural contract, not whether the three new entries
actually fire on the recall cases and stay silent on the lookalikes. The scope note deferred
that live pass to an unnamed "complexity-reduction program", and criterion E5 permits
deferral only to a NAMED ticket.

Named it: `77b6-868f-f4bd-461f` (dissocial-unpleasant-adouri), already linked
`discovered_from` this story. It is the honest owner — it records that the live prompt-eval CI
job scores coverage 0.0 on every spec, so no live calibration can mean anything until it
lands. The gap the reviewer identified is real and now has an owner rather than a program.

### Finding 4 — advisory. Correct, and the deeper problem.

AC5 "deliberately asserts NOTHING about the rubric's prose", while parent epic `77e3`'s AC4
still said "Checked by: `f86e`'s overlay test asserting the taxonomy text is present in the
criterion's rubric". The reviewer's point was precise: the epic's 2026-11-04 comment already
ARGUED for amending that clause, but the clause itself was never edited, so this leaf was
diverging from the parent's authoritative text rather than from a corrected one.

That was a real gap in my sequencing, not a judgement call. Fixed in the stated order —
parent first, then leaf. `77e3`'s AC4 "Checked by" now names this story's calibration corpus
and offline pairing test, with the Rule-5 reasoning recorded in the AC body instead of only
in a comment. Details in `77e3`'s new comment.

Worth stating plainly: the epic's AC4 SUBSTANCE did not change and was not waived. Three of
its five named kinds were measured absent under every synonym, and this story adds all three.
Only the verification method changed, because the original method is forbidden by the artifact
it verifies.

### Not changed

Nothing in the implementation. The commit is untouched at `e5f2b55b740`; `make verify` is at
59% with zero failures and remains valid, since only ticket text changed.

Re-review job `1793828443498618499-c72332fb3fa14520bb09d533720adfd3` is running against the
corrected parent.
